items.note: Press release dated 25 Nov 2021 (title matches). Supports ~600 public surface spaces, start 1 Jan 2022, daily charging, CHF 2.00/h day (7-24h), CHF 1.50/h night (midnight-7am) and Sunday, aim of better-fitting use and more attractive garages, Spelteriniplatz included. Wording problem: the page says charging is 'täglich durchgehend' (all day and night; previously Mon-Fri 8-19h, Sat 8-17h), so 'every day, 7am to midnight' is wrong/contradicts the night rate.
items.corrected_text: The city announced on 25 November 2021 that from 1 January 2022 about 600 public surface parking spaces in the city centre (plus Spelteriniplatz) become fee-paying every day, around the clock, instead of only Monday to Friday 8am-7pm and Saturday 8am-5pm. The rate is CHF 2.00 per hour by day (7am-midnight) and CHF 1.50 per hour at night (midnight-7am) and on Sundays. The city said the aim was to use spaces more appropriately and make underground garages more attractive.

items.note: Read the PDF locally (pypdf). Letter 'Parkiergebühren St.Gallen - Empfehlung des Preisüberwachers', signed 20.03.2024. City press release 'Beschlüsse des Stadtparlaments vom 25. August 2026'. 38-20 (1 abstention) rejection; FDP counter-proposal (no fees Sundays and 12:00-13:30, lower EBZ fees) lost to GLP counter-proposal (no night fees in EBZ) 16-39; final vote refusing to put initiative with GLP counter-proposal to voters 31-28 (1 abstention). The bluewin/blue News article is real and its title matches, and the tariffs quoted (Brühltor and Burggraben CHF 2/h, station garage 2.60, town hall 2.40, Neumarkt 1.50 per half hour for first two half-hours then CHF 2 per 40 min) and the initiative (cut fees ~40-60%, free Sundays and nights 7pm-7am) are in the text. But the draft claim that the page shows no date is wrong: the page metadata gives publication 2026-05-13, consistent with 'since the opening in March last year'. The article text is a blue News rewrite of Tagblatt reporting, and the page carries an automatic 'summary created with' box (we relied on the body text only). Same URL as item 9 - merge.
items.corrected_text: A blue News report (page metadata: published 13 May 2026, based on Tagblatt reporting) describes a 'wild patchwork' of garage tariffs in St. Gallen, citing CHF 2 per hour at Brühltor and Burggraben, CHF 2.60 at the station garage, CHF 2.40 at the town hall and a half-hour system at Neumarkt, and notes that a political initiative proposes cutting fees by about 40-60% and free parking on Sundays and at night (7pm-7am).

items.note: Same article as item 8 (published 2026-05-13 per page metadata). Supported: uniform centre tariff since Nov 2024; Central opened March 2025; first hour CHF 2 but cheaper afterwards, contradicting the 2016 building permit (not lower than surrounding garages, i.e. CHF 2/h); Office for Building Permits sought talks, no agreement; city has been considering legal action for months. Wrong: it is the city (summary) and the president of the Parkleitsystem who call the tariff illegal, not specifically the building-permit office; 'no steps taken yet' overstated - article says it is open when steps will be taken. Date should be 2026-05. Duplicate of item 8's source: merge.
items.corrected_text: The same blue News report (published 13 May 2026 per page metadata) says a uniform parking tariff has applied in the centre since November 2024 and that Parkhaus Central, opened in March 2025, charges CHF 2 for the first hour but less afterwards, contrary to its 2016 building permit (rates not lower than surrounding facilities, i.e. CHF 2 per hour). The president of the parking guidance system calls the tariff illegal and the city is also critical; the Office for Building Permits sought talks with the operators but no agreement has been reached, and the city has been considering legal action for months without it being clear when or how it would act.

items.note: Source returned 403 to curl (bot protection, not bypassed) but could be read through WebFetch, which returned the full article text. Date 3 May 2025 (updated 6 May) matches. The page's own headline was returned as 'BEA und Olma: Publikumsmessen wollen keine Parkplätze', while the URL slug matches the draft title; real <title> could not be confirmed, so title left as is. Content differs from the draft: it is the city of St. Gallen that decided to abolish the Breitfeld car park (not OLMA), about 7,000 vehicles (not visitors) used it last year, over 70% of OLMA guests came by public transport, police said fewer cars had parked there in recent years and that they would watch blue zones closely and reconsider if problems arise.
items.corrected_text: The city of St. Gallen decided to abolish the Breitfeld car park near the Kybunpark stadium that was used for OLMA, which about 7,000 vehicles had used the previous year. The OLMA said over 70% of its guests came by public transport last year; city police said fewer cars had parked there in recent years and that they would monitor residential blue zones closely.

Blick page returned 403 to curl (bot protection, not bypassed) but was readable via WebFetch (full article, 27 Oct 2025, title matches). It is a news report, not an interview, based on Stadtrat Markus Buschor's statements to the St. Galler Tagblatt. Stadtrat backs a third tunnel tube and opposes the Güterbahnhof connection; Stadtparlament removed that part from the city's Richtplan. 'The city rejected the Nov 2024 package' should read: voters in the city of St. Gallen rejected it.
items.corrected_text: In a report published on 27 October 2025, Stadtrat Markus Buschor told the Tagblatt that the St. Gallen city government supports a third Rosenberg tunnel tube but opposes the Güterbahnhof motorway connection; the city parliament had removed that connection from the city's Richtplan. Voters in the city of St. Gallen rejected the November 2024 national road package.

corrected_summary: St. Gallen has charged for about 600 centre surface spaces every day since 1 January 2022, and from 1 November 2024 raised the centre white-zone day rate to CHF 2.50 per hour and introduced night permits in the Extended Blue Zone, after the Swiss Price Supervisor had recommended on 20 March 2024 cutting fees and dropping increases. Fees are now the main political issue: the Stadtparlament rejected the Parkgebühr-Initiative 38 to 20 on 25 August 2026 and a popular vote is scheduled for 28 February 2027, while a second initiative asks for above-ground parking at about 2015 levels (a proposal). Garages are run by a mix of operators (City Parking St. Gallen AG, Indigo Suisse at Neumarkt from 1 April 2025 and listing Parkhaus Central, which opened in March 2025 and is in a tariff dispute with the city), with the Kreuzbleiche garage planned to be renovated from June 2026 to May 2027.
